questions.question: Prove by induction, for integers \(n\geq1\): \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac{n \left(n + 1\right)}{2}\).
questions.questionText: Prove by induction, for integers \(n\geq1\): \(\sum_{r=1}^{n}r=\frac{n \left(n + 1\right)}{2}\).
questions.answer: The formula holds for every integer \(n\geq1\).
steps: Add the next term. In the following algebra, replace n by k: \(\frac{n \left(n + 1\right)}{2}\) + \(n + 1\) = \(\frac{\left(n + 1\right) \left(n + 2\right)}{2}\).
This equals the proposed expression with \(n=k+1\). The base case and inductive implication prove the claim.

questions.answer: The matrix formula holds for all \(n\geq1\).
